checks: Independent A3/A4 and signed-envelope cases now traverse file input, preserving raw RPC, Movement prefix, provenance and later records.
Records consumer error returns the original boxed object and outranks a prefetched later error; no subsequent callback occurs.
Typed later container truncation agrees with slice input; earlier callbacks remain delivered but no successful summary is returned.

Existing tests freshly run on combined Native+Reader cover all truncated preamble/chunk prefixes, maximum admitted info prefix, large Header, bounded read counts, Event stop, skip range checks and schema-limit APIs.
Two independent read-only file cursors avoid shared-offset try_clone behavior; each payload is read by one cursor, apart from the bounded preamble probe.
Sparse skipped-payload proof succeeds under a 512MiB address-space limit; same executable whole-file buffering fails specifically with OutOfMemory.

performance_conclusion.review_scope: Recomputed each recorded pair, medians, CPU utilization and CPU totals; checked report hashes, before/after provenance, control and reverse-label executable identities, six Reader parity entries, 60 export receipts and 668 recorded Parquet fingerprints. No fresh benchmark or actual export reread performed in this review.

limits: Linux local QA does not substitute for final hosted Windows/Linux, feature matrix, rustdoc, Clippy, Python and replay CI.
Six real replay file/slice parity entries are author executions reviewed for consistency, not six independent combined-source decodes.
CLI and Parquet file loading remain unchanged; the accepted Reader improvement is input memory use, with no stable speed improvement claimed.
Memory scales with encoded/current/prefetched chunks, full Event/Header payloads and parser/consumer state; no fixed global cap.
Consumer stop prevents further callbacks; scoped worker can finish current decoding or scan a header-only tail before joining, without a bounded cancellation-time guarantee.
Files must remain unchanged during reading; same-length concurrent writes or replacement are outside the documented snapshot guarantee.
Sparse proof is synthetic, skips payloads and does not establish large decoded-chunk memory bounds.
